messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a Terraform change to move the GPU ASG in us-west-2 to a mixed on-demand + spot (preemptible) pool. Goal: ~25–35% infra cost reduction while keeping p95 latency SLOs. Plan sketch below, want 👀 before I start the rollout.

kevin: Nice. Are we doing lowest-price or capacity-optimized for allocation?

maria: Capacity-optimized. We saw too much churn with lowest-price in eu-west. Strategy: prefer capacity-optimized across families, explicit list of prioritized families (p4d, p4de, p3dn, g5, g5g), fallback to on-demand above base capacity. Multi-AZ.

jia: Interruption handling is my main concern — we can't lose KV cache or long-lived encoder state on preempt. What's the graceful drain plan?

maria: Good call. We'll wire ASG lifecycle hooks -> termination handler daemonset on k8s that: 1) receives spot interruption (2-minute notice) 2) cordons + drains pods, 3) triggers in-cluster cache warmup to replicas (redis fallback) and 4) notifies routing to stop sending new requests. Also add a small preempt buffer (keep 1-2 on-demand per AZ as base). Terraform will create the lifecycle hook + an sns -> lambda for older clusters that don't support the daemonset. Snippet: 

```terraform
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_asg" {
  name                      = "gpu-mixed-asg"
  mixed_instances_policy {
    launch_template {
      launch_template_specification {
        launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id
        version            = "$Latest"
      }
    }
    instances_distribution {
      on_demand_base_capacity                  = 2
      on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 25
      spot_instance_pools                      = 6
      spot_allocation_strategy                 = "capacity-optimized"
    }
  }
  desired_capacity = var.desired_gpu_capacity
  min_size        = var.min_gpu_capacity
  max_size        = var.max_gpu_capacity
  tags = [
    { key = "Environment" , value = var.env, propagate_at_launch = true },
    { key = "Service" , value = "inference-gpu", propagate_at_launch = true },
    { key = "Lifecycle", value = "spot-mixed", propagate_at_launch = true },
  ]
}
```

sam: AMI rotation? We need deterministic AMIs for reproducible kernels / drivers.

maria: We'll use versioned AMI tags baked by Packer: `redwood-gpu-ami:vYYYY-MM-DD-<build>`. TF uses a data lookup by tag to set `image_id`. AMI bake pipeline will run smoke tests (cuda, nccl) and publish a short changelog.

kevin: Testing & rollout plan? Canary first?

maria: Canary in us-west-2a with 20% of the capacity for 6 hours of staged load. Steps: 1) apply TF to canary ASG only, 2) run replayed production traffic via `replicate-load` job, 3) monitor p95 latency, drop rate, preempt events, 4) if metrics stable, roll to remaining AZs. Rollout gated by feature flag in ops repo `enable_mixed_spot_pool`.

jia: Also add tags for cost attribution — product, team, env, owner — and ensure billing export picks them up. And watch ENI counts, mixed pools spawn more instances quickly.

maria: Yep: `tags` include `product`, `team`, `env`, `lifecycle=spot-mixed`. Added a quota check in the plan step to fail if projected ENI > quota. Also added a TTL backoff for spot replacement so we don't thrash on mass interruptions.

kevin: Can we have a hard fallback route? If spot saturation or interruption rate > 30% for 15m, shift traffic to dedicated pool?

maria: Yes — plan includes `fallback_pool = "dedicated-gpu-reserve"` and a small control-plane automation that flips routing policies (service mesh weight) when avg preempt rate > threshold. Will be an ops toggle first, then automated.

sre-bot: terraform plan executed for canary at 1743629220 — 1 plan, 0 applies yet. Warnings: 3 (deprecated instance type in eu-west-1).

sam: One more: networking config in the launch template — set `interface` to use ENA and set driver params in userdata. Also add cloud-init steps to pre-warm NVMe.

maria: Good call, adding userdata snippet: `#!/bin/bash\nmodprobe ena\n/etc/init.d/nvme_warmup start` in template. Also added `Placement Group = spread` as opt for stability.

kevin: :thumbsup: Looks solid. Can you open the PR with the TF changes and the rollout playbook? I'll review the canary logs asap.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/412 — includes plan, playbook, step-by-step rollback. Tagging reviewers @kevin @jia @sam. :shipit:

sre-bot: Plan applied to canary cluster at 1743629775 — resources: 3 created, 2 changed, 0 destroyed. Monitor for spot interruptions for the next 6h.
